column1: # Traduzione inglese dei testi del corso Tongji (esercizi di completamento e frasi da riordinare).

column2: Do you know the teacher’s phone number?
知道 = to know (a piece of information).
Which building do you live in?
你怎么了 = what’s the matter with you?
She’s ill, she can’t come to class today.
能 = can, to be able to.
Why are you only getting here now? It’s nine o’clock!
The alarm clock stopped, so I arrived late.
I’d like to ask for half a day off.
请 + length of time + 假.
A不A: yes/no question without 吗.
In alternative questions you use 还是 (或者 is used in statements).
At the market weight is counted in 斤.
Adjective + 一点儿 = a bit more…
Sit down, there are some snacks on the table: help yourself.
随便 = as you like, freely.
Since I came to China I’ve got used to tea.
Can you finish half a jin of dumplings?
呢 at the end of a sentence = action in progress.
V1 + 着 + V2: two simultaneous actions.
有点儿 + verb/adjective, for something negative.
I think he’s a good student.
觉得 = to think, to feel.
Can you answer this question? — Of course!
Why aren’t you coming to class?
I’m going to the library to borrow books.
I went to the library, but I didn’t manage to borrow that book.
没 V 到 = not to manage to get.
Just fill in the delivery form.
V + 一下 = briefly, for a moment.
The parcel arrived as early as this morning.
就 + 了 = sooner than expected (才 doesn’t go with 了).
What time does the library close?
You give me fifty, I give you ten back.
怎么样 asks what a situation is like.
I heard you were ill: are you better now?
Are you busy with your studies? — So-so.
Autumn here is especially nice, neither cold nor hot.
How long are the winter holidays?
一月 = January; 一个月 = one month.
I only have three subjects, that’s not many.
没 + V + 过 = never to have done.
去……怎么走? = how do you get to…?
The bank is right there on the right side of the road.
It isn’t far, you’ll be there in five minutes.
I’m not sure, ask someone else.
不清楚 = I don’t know exactly.
The dentist is on the second floor.
The food here is good and cheap.
位 = polite measure word for people.
Waiter, two bottles of beer, please!
来 = to bring / to have (at a restaurant).
Is one bowl of rice enough?
I’m full, I can’t eat any more.
吃饱 = to eat your fill.
We ordered fish, meat, soup and so on.
V + 得 + adjective = complement of degree.
Starting next week I’ll practise for an hour a day.
You must come tomorrow! — OK, I’ll definitely come.
What’s your hobby? — I like travelling.
I go to the library twice a week.
Go home and get some proper rest.
To 对不起 you reply 没关系.
The exam went badly: I didn’t prepare well.
Stop joking, he’s not my boyfriend!
I want to go out for a walk, come with me.
陪 = to accompany, to keep company.
I like reading, listening to music…
You really are a good student!
真是个… = you really are a…
Going round the shops is tiring, studying is even more tiring.
What do you usually do at the weekend?
This mountain is high: climbing it is tiring.
There’s a mountain near the school.
座 = measure word for mountains and buildings.
I came to China last year.
As long as you practise every day, you’ll learn well.
Class is about to start, let’s go.
My phone is dead: I forgot to charge it.
Don’t just look at the pinyin: look at the characters more.
张 = measure word for flat objects.
Characters are too hard: I’m afraid I won’t manage to learn them.
This is the lesson I like most.
Weren’t you leaving? Why are you still here?
I thought there was class today, but there isn’t.
俩 = two (people), without a measure word.
Sometimes I take the bus, sometimes I cycle.
有时候……有时候…… = sometimes… sometimes…
It’s cold today: you need to wear your down jacket.
穿 = to wear (clothes, shoes); 戴 = glasses, hats.
This top is a bit tight: is there a large size?
I tried on three, but they still don’t fit.
还是 = still, all the same.
My size isn’t available? Never mind, I won’t buy it.
It’s getting colder day by day.
一天比一天 = day by day.
没有一 + MW + …的 = not a single one.
It’s not that the dress is expensive: it’s that I didn’t bring any money.
I’ll go when I have time.
The forecast says it will rain tomorrow.
How many people are there in your family?
口 = measure word for family members.
My sister is at middle school.
You look a lot like your mother.
My father works in a hospital: he’s a doctor.
The girl at the back dressed in red is my older sister.
If you come to my house, they’ll definitely welcome you.
As soon as the holidays start, I’m going home.
然后 links two actions in sequence; 以后 usually follows a verb (吃饭以后).
I’m thinking of staying in Yunnan for about ten days.
The semester is about to end.
Tickets for the Spring Festival are hard to get: you need to book early.
My name is Wang Ping, I’m Chinese.
It’s time for you to go to class.
I have no class at eight today.
In the afternoon there’s listening class from 2:00 to 3:50.
Excuse me, where is the canteen?
The toilet is to the right of the classroom.
The dormitory is to the left of the canteen.
Does this kind of bike come in white?
Let’s buy him a present together.
I want to go back to my room to rest.
Tomorrow I have to go to the embassy.
I’d like to ask for two days off.
I wasn’t used to drinking tea before.
Let’s chat while listening to some music.
I think he’s a bit down.
Please fill in the delivery form.
I didn’t manage to get that book.
The book has arrived at my dormitory.
I heard you’ve got a cold.
I’ve already got used to it.
I’ve been to the Great Wall twice.
How long have you studied Chinese?
Our winter holidays are in January.
It’s the first time I’ve had Peking duck.
It’s just a few minutes’ walk.
The bank is on the left side of the road.
Excuse me, where do they sell shoes?
We’ll have the tomato and egg.
We can’t finish it: let’s take it away.
I’d like you to be my tutor.
